html:
The founding of Syracuse, in eastern Sicily, by colonists from Corinth led by Archias, around 734 BCE. They settled first on the small island of Ortygia, which had a fresh spring and two good harbours.

It was one of the early cities of Greek colonisation in the west. Syracuse grew rich on grain and trade, and became the largest Greek city in the west, a rival to Carthage for control of Sicily.

Its later history is full of big names:

  • Gelon defeated Carthage at the Battle of Himera in 480 BCE.
  • Syracuse destroyed the Athenian army in the Sicilian Expedition of 415 to 413 BCE.
  • Dionysius I made it the capital of a great western power.
  • The mathematician Archimedes defended it against Rome, which took it in 212 BCE.
